title: Checks for large const arrays that should be defined as static instead.
summary: Performance: const variables are inlined upon use. Static items result in only one instance and has a fixed location in memory. Clippy puts this lint in the perf group, at the level warn.

title: Warns if the digits of an integral or floating-point constant are grouped into groups that are too large.
summary: Negatively impacts readability. Clippy puts this lint in the pedantic group, at the level allow.

title: Checks for large size differences between variants on enums.
summary: Enum size is bounded by the largest variant. Having one large variant can penalize the memory layout of that enum. Clippy puts this lint in the perf group, at the level warn.

title: It checks for the size of a Future created by async fn or async {}.
summary: Due to the current unideal implementation of Coroutine, large size of a Future may cause stack overflows. Clippy puts this lint in the pedantic group, at the level allow.

title: Checks for the inclusion of large files via include_bytes!() or include_str!().
summary: Including large files can undesirably increase the size of the binary produced by the compiler. This lint may be used to catch mistakes where an unexpectedly large file is included, or temporarily to obtain a list of all large files. Clippy puts this lint in the restriction group, at the level allow.

title: Checks for local arrays that may be too large.
summary: Large local arrays may cause stack overflow. Clippy puts this lint in the pedantic group, at the level allow.

title: Checks for functions that use a lot of stack space.
summary: The stack region of memory is very limited in size (usually much smaller than the heap) and attempting to use too much will result in a stack overflow and crash the program. To avoid this, you should consider allocating large types on the heap instead (e.g. by boxing them). Clippy puts this lint in the nursery group, at the level allow.

title: Checks for functions taking arguments by value, where the argument type is Copy and large enough to be worth considering passing by reference.
summary: Does not trigger if the function is being exported, because that might induce API breakage, if the parameter is declared as mutable, or if the argument is a self. Arguments passed by value might result in an unnecessary shallow copy, taking up more space in the stack and requiring a call to memcpy, which can be expensive. Clippy puts this lint in the pedantic group, at the level allow.
